world.bio: Run a six-person demolition and strip-out crew in Brunswick, Melbourne. We gut old terraces and sheds, mostly for renovators and small builders. Twenty-five years in the trade and my back reminds me daily. I hate throwing good timber in a skip but can't afford to do anything else with it. Coach my daughter's netball team and restore a 1972 Holden Kingswood in the garage.
skills_assets: Licensed demolition contractor, asbestos awareness, white card, working at heights
Two tip trucks, a bobcat, a mini excavator, scaffolding and a dust extraction rig
Six-person crew, two of them with 15+ years
Knowledge of period houses: Victorian, Edwardian and 1930s construction, what's under the lino and what is behind the plaster
Last week we pulled about three cubic metres of 1890s Baltic pine and Tasmanian blackwood out of a Carlton terrace; the boards are still stacked in my yard under a tarp
Contacts with a couple of architects and one salvage yard in Thornbury

projects.name: Carlton terrace strip-out
projects.text: Two-storey terrace, three weeks. We removed the 1970s kitchen extension, ripped out ceilings and opened up the floors. Underneath were hand-planed 1890s Baltic pine floorboards and some Tasmanian blackwood skirting. Beautiful stuff, though riddled with nails and covered in decades of bitumen glue. Tip fees for that type of timber are $140 a tonne plus a $400 skip hire. It's killing the margins.

projects.name: Brunswick warehouse fit-out job
projects.text: Strip a former textile warehouse into an open-plan office. Eight working days. Mostly steel and brick, which is easier to handle. Client wants everything gone by 15 October.

projects.name: 1972 Kingswood restoration
projects.text: Rebuilding the 253 V8 engine in the garage. Waiting on a gasket set from Adelaide. Not touched in three weeks.

notes.text: Lower back out today. Took two Panadol and sat in the ute for lunch. The young bloke Jaz did the heavy lifting. He's got potential, but he won't wear his dust mask without me yelling.

Carlton job. Pulled up the floor in the front room and found the Baltic pine. Spent an hour on my knees just looking at it. 140 years old, and not a single board warped. These houses were built by people who gave a damn. Customer said 'throw it all out'. I said 'let me think about it'.

Tip fees up again. Counted the weekly bill: $3,100 on tip fees alone. For what? Perfectly good timber that gets chipped into mulch. Can't I even give it to someone? I tried listing on Facebook Marketplace: five people messaged, two said 'is it free', one asked for delivery to Geelong.
Netball practice. Our goal attack, Ruby, hit six from six. The mum next to me said 'is your husband coming?' I said 'I'm the dad'. She went red. I said it happens.

Called a salvage yard in Thornbury. He said 'we don't take nailed stock, too much hassle, and the market's slow'. I asked what he'd pay if I de-nailed it. He said 'maybe $200 a cubic metre'. That's 600 bucks for three cubes and two days of my crew's time.
Wife thinks I'm obsessed with the timber. Maybe I am. My old man was a carpenter. He would've cried at the sight of the stuff going in the skip. I stacked the best boards in the yard under a tarp.
Insurance renewal due. Premium up 18 percent. I keep paying for things that don't make me money.

Carlton job finished. Skips gone. Timber stacked in the yard: about three cubes, mostly decent length, plenty of nails. Architect friend Dave dropped by and said 'you should talk to some furniture makers'. I said I don't know any.

messages.text: Karen: Don't forget Ruby's game at 10. Me: I'll be there. Karen: And the tarp on the yard stuff is flapping. Me: I'll fix it. Karen: You're hoarding wood. Me: It's not hoarding if it's beautiful.
Jaz: Boss, what do we do with the pine? Me: Stack it. Jaz: In the yard? Me: Yep. Jaz: It's gonna rot. Me: Tarp it.
Dave: Ray, that's gorgeous timber. Me: Yeah. Dave: Salvage's your best bet. Me: They want it de-nailed and priced like firewood. Dave: Maybe a maker would do better.
Client: Is all the rubbish gone? Me: Yes. Client: The invoice seems high with the extra tip fees. Me: It was heavier than quoted. Client: Fair enough.

relations.about: Wife, nurse, says Ray's yard looks like a lumberyard.
Young crew member, 22, keen but careless.
Architect mate from the footy club.

constraints: Margins are thin, can't spend more than half a day of crew time de-nailing
Yard space limited, timber must be moved within two months
Doesn't do online listings that need lots of messaging
sensitive: Feels guilty about timber waste, thinks of his father

disclosure_policy.t0_public: Melbourne demolition contractor; recently recovered 1890s Baltic pine and Tasmanian blackwood from a Carlton terrace.
disclosure_policy.t1_after_signal: Quantities, condition of the timber, tip-fee pressure, timeline for moving it.
